clue.text: Journalist unknown, in poverty, reported fights dear to a 6

parts.note: a hack is a slang word for a journalist

indicators.note: the unknown is placed inside the word for poverty

parts.note: need means want or poverty
Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard rather than read, so it is given by its sound

parts.note: frays are fights or brawls

explanation.surface: A reporter, broke and down at heel, is said to have got into scraps that some pompous person cherishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is a cross-reference to 6 Down, PLATITUDINARIAN: a lover of stale, trite remarks would hold such a worn-out expression dear.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude-lover treasures any stale, overused expression, the very kind of cliché meant here.

clue.text: Fine food old hooligan leader gets in Yorkshire

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
lamb is a meat, so a food
a rough is a rowdy thug
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: Fine dining for an elderly yob boss turns up somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: FLAMBOROUGH HEAD is a chalk headland on the Yorkshire coast of England; the definition simply places it.
explanation.definitionFit: The headland lies on the North Sea coast of the English county, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Relative grasps the point; cat getting butter would make an earth mover's record

indicators.note: grasps means the relative's letters hold the point inside them

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative
E is a compass point, east
mog is British slang for a cat
a ram butts, so it is a butter in the cryptic sense

explanation.surface: A family member takes the point while the cat gets the butter, oddly linked to digging-machine paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts, a RAM. An 'earth mover' is not a digger but an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: A seismic chart traces ground tremors, so it is the written trace left by a quake that shook the earth.

clue.text: Note I'd put up following one on church building

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the letters read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: the letters of I'd, apostrophe dropped
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
I is the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A memo is pinned up after a sole notice on the church building.
explanation.definitionFit: An edifice is a large, imposing structure, a synonym for a building.

clue.text: Joke about name of band

indicators.note: about means the joke's letters go round the other letter

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Someone makes a joke about what a music group is called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a music group, as the surface suggests, but here it means a group of people or a crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang and a band are both groups of people acting together, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Lover of the 1 put initial A and R in the wrong place

indicators.note: letters set down in the wrong place have been rearranged, signalling an anagram

parts.note: the fifteen letters of these words make up the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap the opening A and the R reads like a typesetter's correction.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is a cross-reference to 1 Down, HACKNEYED PHRASE: someone who loves trite expressions loves platitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitudinarian is someone given to uttering trite commonplaces, so a fan of clichés.

clue.text: Musician's inner circle, frantically busy, get to drink at the charity event

indicators.note: inner means the circle sits inside the musicians' word

parts.note: read as musicians, a band of players
a ring is a circle

indicators.note: doing something frantically suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: ale is a drink, a beer

explanation.surface: A performer's close friends, rushed off their feet, are off for a drink at a fund-raiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranged by 'frantically' gives BUYS. 'Musician's' must be read as musicians, a BAND, which holds RING. A BRING-AND-BUY SALE is a British charity sale where people bring items to sell and buy others'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fund-raising sale where donors both supply goods and purchase them, a typical charity event.

clue.text: Old actor put the kibosh on side wall

parts.note: Clark Gable was a Hollywood star of the 1930s and 40s
to put the kibosh on something is to end it

explanation.surface: A veteran film star stops something dead beside a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A gable end is the end wall of a building under the triangular gable, often a side wall.

clue.text: Being completely taken aback, girl admits the sport's attraction

indicators.note: the whole assembly, not just one piece, is turned back to front
admits means the girl's name takes the sport inside it

parts.note: Ella is a girl's name
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A girl, utterly stunned, lets in what draws people to the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'completely taken aback' turns the whole container, ERULLA, round; 'Being' and the possessive are only link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is charm or appeal, the power of attraction.

clue.text: Cuts it fine and misses about a million

indicators.note: about means the word for misses goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: skips means misses out or omits
M is the abbreviation for a million

explanation.surface: Someone leaves things late and fails to win a million.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts it fine' suggests leaving little time; here it means economising too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to be stingy, spending or providing too little, cutting things too fine.

clue.text: Disturbed night after fellow soldier's return to combat

indicators.note: after places the scrambled night behind the other letters
return means the soldier's letters are turned back

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: disturbed means put into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restless night follows a comrade's homecoming from battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting and combat both name armed struggle between foes, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Check duck in bar

parts.note: to vet something is to check or examine it
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Inspect the duck served in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is the verb meaning to forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto a proposal is to forbid or block it, so it is a synonym of the verb bar.

clue.text: The corral's shambolic, but from it comes such music

indicators.note: shambolic means chaotic and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped, are the fodder

explanation.surface: A chaotic cattle pen nonetheless produces symphonic sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written for or played by a symphony band of strings, brass and woodwind is described this way.

clue.text: Vanishing weathercocks in the city point to extremes of neglect

indicators.note: in places the weathercocks inside the city's letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
vanes are weathercocks, devices showing wind direction
E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Weathervanes disappearing in town reveal signs of neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: Evanescent means fading quickly from sight, so it is a synonym of vanishing.

clue.text: 5 of villains came down, it's said, over the tracks

indicators.note: it's said means the phrase is heard aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: came down on is fell on
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the tracks

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have tumbled onto the railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is a cross-reference to 5 Down, GANG. 'came down... over' gives FELL ON, which sounds like FELON.
explanation.definitionFit: Felonry is a collective term for criminals, a body of outlaws.

clue.text: A French book found in the "Music and Ideas" section

indicators.note: found in the means the answer's letters sit inside the quoted phrase

explanation.surface: A Gallic volume turns up in the music and ideas part of a library.
explanation.walkthrough: CANDIDE is Voltaire's satirical French novel of 1759.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire's novel is a classic book written in French.

clue.text: Coarse about it being a military expedition

indicators.note: about means the coarse word goes round the other letters

parts.note: crude means coarse or vulgar
it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A vulgar remark about it surfaces on a military campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade was a medieval military expedition, especially to the Holy Land.

clue.text: Pet guru Mae delivered from a sticky situation

indicators.note: delivered suggests the letters are freed and set out anew in another order

parts.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: An animal expert called Mae rescued someone from a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: UP A GUM TREE is a British idiom for being in trouble with no way out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone stuck in a predicament, which is a sticky spot.

clue.text: Common sense from which we are excluded?

parts.note: a no to someone shuts them out
us is the object form of we

explanation.surface: A wry question about a kind of good judgement that leaves the speakers out.
explanation.walkthrough: Something 'from which we are excluded' is NO US. NOUS is British informal for practical good sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is practical intelligence, everyday good sense.

clue.text: Past history of nettle rash following slight curve

indicators.note: following places the rash word after the curve word

parts.note: an arc is part of a curve
hives is a skin rash, also called nettle rash

explanation.surface: An itchy rash has a long record after a small bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are stored records, the documents of history.

clue.text: Sackville-West gets up at 4

indicators.note: in a down clue gets up means the letters rise, so they read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An English writer rises early at four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4 Down but is just the number. Vita Sackville-West was an English writer and gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: Vita was the first name of the writer Sackville-West.

clue.text: Drop in respect?

parts.note: a drop here is a bob or dip of the knees made out of respect, not a decline

explanation.surface: A fall in esteem is suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsy is a brief bending of the knees as a mark of deference.

clue.text: A point of view not quite on the level

parts.note: a slant is an angle or point of view

explanation.surface: An opinion that is not entirely honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at an angle, so not quite horizontal.

clue.text: "New laid" has been, and can be, refuted

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim about freshly laid eggs that has been and can be disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deniable means able to be denied, i.e. refuted.
